# Load data

Starting from by_GRB_list. Elements in the list are GRBs named by their
genomic range. !!! Do not try to view the whole list since it has no
print limit and will crash R.!!! Each GRB element contains four other
elements:

1.  DF of genes inside the GRB with ensembl and hgnc ids. Also each gene
    is categorized as one of the following:

    ![](images/paste-FEDAF3F1.png)

2.  DF where rownames are enhancer regions and columns are transcripts.
    Values in the df represent **correlation** between expression levels
    from the cage experiment. It contains values from -1 to 1. (t*his
    dataframe will not be used since it is not informational - Anja
    mail*)

3.  DF with rownames as enhancer regions and columns are transcripts.
    Values
    in the df contain values of the permutation test. The description of
    the test in my (physical) notebook. It contains values from 0 to 1.


## Helper functions
This is a helper function. Not sure if useful.
```{r}
namedVecToDf <- function(named_vector, column_name = "col1"){
  df <- as.data.frame(named_vector) %>%

    dplyr::select({{column_name}} := Var1, Freq)
  return(df)
}
```

Helper function for bining the right part of histograms.
```{r}
calcHistogramDataMaxBin <- function(data_, max_bin){
  # Input data vector for the histogram
  # returns frequency data that can be plotted with bar plots
  # This handles only numerical values and the function bins values > max_bin
  
  # Frequency table
  data_tb <- table(data_) %>% as.data.frame()
  # Summing up rows from max_bin to the end
  total_ <- data_tb[(max_bin+1):dim(data_tb)[1], "Freq"] %>%
    sum()
  
  # Selecting first n data
  res_ <- data_tb[0:max_bin,] %>%
    mutate(data_= as.character(data_))
  # Adding the info from the rest
  res_ <- rbind(res_,c("rest", total_)) %>%
    select(x=data_, Freq)
  # Locking positions? 
  res_$x <- factor(res_$x, levels = res_$x)
  
  
  
  return(res_)
}
```

Calculates number of data points in boxplots
```{r}
give.n <- function(x){
  return(c(y = -0.5, label = length(x))) 
  # experiment with the multiplier to find the perfect position
}
```


A enhancer_transcript_df table is built in a way that a combination of
gene:transcript id and an enhancer range is the key (unique
combination). Every such pair has an empirical p value calculated via
permutation test. Other columns derived from the by_GRB_list are:

-   **grb:** range of the GRB which span the genes and enhancers

-   **ensembl:** gene ensembl id, there may be multiple transcripts per
    gene

-   **symbol:** hgnc gene symbol

-   **category:** gene category which depends whether it is mapped by
    the GWAS catalog and by the GRB hypothesis

Additional features:

-   **enh_num_4gene:** number of enhancers that regulate that gene

-   **gene_num_4enh:** number of genes that are under regulation by that
    enhancer.

Looping through all grb's in the by_GRB_list to fetch all df.
## Creating enhancer_transcript_df
```{r CREATE enhancer_transcript_df, eval=TRUE}
enhancer_transcript_df <- data.frame()
empty_grbs <- c()
for(i in 1:length(by_GRB_list)){
  message(paste(i,". Binding the grb: ",names(by_GRB_list)[i], sep = ""))
  working_el <- by_GRB_list[[i]]
  
  if(setequal(dim(by_GRB_list[[i]][[3]]) ,c(0,0))){
    message(paste(i,". does not have enhancers", sep=""))
    empty_grbs <- append(empty_grbs, names(by_GRB_list)[i])
    next
  }
  
  # Df for the ith grb
  working_df <- 
  data.frame(
    # Adding GRB coordinates
    grb = names(by_GRB_list)[i],
    # This column contains gene id, transcript id and enhancer from df3
    gene_trans_enh = c(outer(colnames(working_el[[3]]),rownames(working_el[[3]]), FUN=paste, sep="_")),
    
    # Unrolling emp values in a vector and adding them to the enhancer_transcript_df
    emp = as.vector(t(as.matrix(working_el[[3]])))
    ) %>%
    
    # Splitting gene:transcript ids and enhancer location
    dplyr::mutate(gene_trans=str_split(gene_trans_enh, pattern="_", simplify=TRUE)[,1],
           enh=str_split(gene_trans_enh, pattern="_", simplify=TRUE)[,2]) %>%
      
    # Splitting gene and transcript ids - ensembl gene id
    dplyr:: mutate(ensembl=str_split(gene_trans, pattern=":", simplify=TRUE)[,1]) %>%
      
    # Splitting gene and transcript ids - ensembl transcript id
    dplyr::mutate(transcript=str_split(gene_trans, pattern=":", simplify=TRUE)[,2]) %>%
      
    # Adding gene symbol and category
    left_join(working_el[[1]], by=c("ensembl"="ens")) %>%
    
    # Removing the extra column
    dplyr::select(-gene_trans_enh)
  
  if(any(working_df$emp < 0.001)){
  

    working_df <- working_df %>%
    # Adding per enhancer number of genes that it regulates (emp < 0.001)
      left_join(as.data.frame(base::table(filter(working_df, emp < 0.001)$enh)), 
                by = c("enh" = "Var1")) %>%
    dplyr::rename(gene_num_4enh=Freq) %>%
    
    # Adding per gene number of enh that are regulated by (emp < 0.001)
    left_join(as.data.frame(base::table(filter(working_df, emp < 0.001)$transcript)), 
              by = c("transcript" = "Var1")) %>%
    dplyr::rename(enh_num_4gene=Freq)
    
  }
  else{
    working_df$gene_num_4enh <- NA
    working_df$enh_num_4gene <- NA
  }
  
  
    
  # Apending rows to enhancer_transcript_df
  enhancer_transcript_df <- rbind(enhancer_transcript_df, working_df)
  
}

# Adding ranges from R object - provided by Filip
enhancer_transcript_df <-
  enhancer_transcript_df %>%
  dplyr::left_join(enh_trans_ranges, by = c("enh","transcript"))

rm(enh_trans_ranges)

# Setting 0 on number of interactions to non significant associations
enhancer_transcript_df <- enhancer_transcript_df %>%
  mutate(gene_num_4enh = ifelse(is.na(gene_num_4enh), 0, gene_num_4enh),
         enh_num_4gene = ifelse(is.na(enh_num_4gene), 0, enh_num_4gene))

# saveRDS(enhancer_transcript_df, file.path(project_dir, processed_dir, "by_GRB_list_enh_trans_df.rds"))
saveRDS(enhancer_transcript_df, filename)
```

## Boxplots
Genes are sorted in 5 bins by categories. Each gene (transcript) has an number of enhancers that they are associated with. In this boxplot we compare by category how many enhancers are assigned to each bin.
### per transcript
```{r}
# Subsetting unique transcripts
per_transcript <- enhancer_transcript_df %>%
  #filter(emp < 0.001) %>%
  select(grb, ensembl, symbols=symbol, transcript, category, enh_num_4gene) %>%
  unique()


ggplot(per_transcript, aes(x=category, y=enh_num_4gene, fill=category)) +
  geom_boxplot()+
  theme_minimal() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0,20))+
    stat_summary(fun = "median", geom = "crossbar", color = "yellow", size = 0.4, show.legend = FALSE)+
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "crossbar", color = "gray", size = 0.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = give.n, geom = "text")+
  scale_fill_manual(values = GRB_CAT_COLORS)+
  ggtitle("Boxplot of num enhancers associated with transcript per category")


ggplot(per_transcript, aes(x=category, y=enh_num_4gene, fill=category)) +
  geom_violin()+
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0,20))+ 
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = GRB_CAT_COLORS)+
  stat_summary(fun.data = give.n, geom = "text")+
  stat_summary(fun = "median", geom = "crossbar", color = "yellow", size = 0.4, show.legend = FALSE)+
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "crossbar", color = "gray", size = 0.4, show.legend = FALSE)+
  ggtitle("Violin of num enhancers associated with transcript per category")
```

Binning gene-enhancer ranges.
```{r}
enhancer_transcript_df <-
  enhancer_transcript_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ranges_binned = case_when(
    enh_trans_range <= 1000 ~ "1-10^3",
    enh_trans_range > 1000 & enh_trans_range <= 10000 ~ "10^3-10^4",
    enh_trans_range > 10000 & enh_trans_range <= 100000 ~ "10^4-10^5",
    enh_trans_range > 100000 & enh_trans_range <= 1000000 ~ "10^5-10^6",
    enh_trans_range > 1000000 ~ "10^6-"))
```

# EP count distance category - Counting enhancer - promoter (EP) pair per category and distance bin

Here we count enhancers that regulate a gene selecting only those with p value < 0.001 (or some other).
From the enhancer_transcript_df df that contains values of each enh-gene emp values we first separate them by ranges as defined above. Then, per range bin we count how many enhancers regulate a gene(transcript). To visualize that we separate genes by category status they have in GRB. As explained above.

```{r}
# Counts per EP distance bin number of singf. EP pairs
EP_pair_count <- 
  enhancer_transcript_df %>%
  filter(emp < 0.001) %>%
  group_by(transcript, ranges_binned) %>%
  count(transcript) %>%
  select(enh_num_4gene_binned = n, everything())

enhancer_transcript_df <- left_join(enhancer_transcript_df, EP_pair_count)

enhancer_transcript_df <- enhancer_transcript_df %>%
  mutate(enh_num_4gene_binned = ifelse(is.na(enh_num_4gene_binned), 0, enh_num_4gene_binned))
```
## Ploting EP count-dist-cat bins
```{r}
ep_categories <- 
  enhancer_transcript_df %>%
         #filter(emp < 0.001) %>% 
         select(transcript, category, enh_num_4gene_binned, ranges_binned) %>% 
         unique()

ggplot(ep_categories,
       aes(x=category, y=enh_num_4gene_binned, fill=category)) +
  geom_violin(adjust = 2)+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.text.x=element_blank())+
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.5,5))+
  facet_wrap(~ranges_binned, scales = "free", nrow = 2, ncol = 3)+
  ggtitle("Number of enhancers per gene by category")+
  stat_summary(fun = "median", geom = "crossbar", color = "yellow", size = 0.4, show.legend = FALSE)+
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "crossbar", color = "gray", size = 0.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = give.n, geom = "text")+
  # Adding colors to categories
  scale_fill_manual(values = GRB_CAT_COLORS)
```

### t test 
```{r}
for(i in enhancer_transcript_df_sub$ranges_binned %>% unique() %>% sort){
  x = filter(enhancer_transcript_df_sub, ranges_binned == i & target_gene == "No")$enh_num_4gene_binned
  y = filter(enhancer_transcript_df_sub, ranges_binned == i & target_gene == "Yes")$enh_num_4gene_binned
  print(paste("Interval", i))
  print(wilcox.test(x,y, alternative = "greater"))
}
```
## Cumulative EP count-dist-cat
Summing up EP pairs per distance bins
```{r}

EP_pair_count <- 
  enhancer_transcript_df %>%
  filter(emp < 0.001) %>%
  select(transcript, ranges_binned, enh_num_4gene_binned) %>%
  unique() %>% 
  arrange(ranges_binned)%>%
  group_by(transcript) %>%
  mutate("cm_enh_num_4gene" = cumsum(enh_num_4gene_binned))

enhancer_transcript_df <- 
  left_join(enhancer_transcript_df, EP_pair_count)

# Changing NA to 0
enhancer_transcript_df <- enhancer_transcript_df %>%
  mutate(cm_enh_num_4gene = ifelse(is.na(cm_enh_num_4gene), 0, cm_enh_num_4gene))

print("Example")
enhancer_transcript_df %>%
  filter(emp < 0.001 & transcript =="ENST00000308873") %>%
  select(symbol, transcript, ranges_binned, enh_num_4gene_binned, cm_enh_num_4gene) %>%
  unique() %>%
  arrange(ranges_binned)
```

```{r}
  theme(axis.text.x=element_blank())+
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.5,15))+
  facet_wrap(~ranges_binned, scales = "free", nrow = 2, ncol = 3)+
  ggtitle("Number of enhancers per transcript by category cumulative")+
  #geom_text(data = enhancer_transcript_df, aes(x=category, y = 0))+
  stat_summary(fun.data = give.n, geom = "text")+
  stat_summary(fun = "median", geom = "crossbar", color = "yellow", size = 0.4, show.legend = FALSE)+
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "crossbar", color = "gray", size = 0.4, show.legend = FALSE)+
  # Adding colors to categories
  scale_fill_manual(values = GRB_CAT_COLORS)
```
Target genes

```{r}
# Subseting for plots (use unique combinations not the enhancer_transcript_df table which is full)
enhtrans_sub <- enhancer_transcript_df %>%

ggplot(enhtrans_sub, aes(x=target_gene, y=cm_enh_num_4gene,fill=target_gene))+

```

### t test
```{r}
for(i in enhancer_transcript_df$ranges_binned %>% unique() %>% sort){
  x = filter(enhtrans_sub, ranges_binned == i & target_gene == "No")$cm_enh_num_4gene
  y = filter(enhtrans_sub, ranges_binned == i & target_gene == "Yes")$cm_enh_num_4gene
  print(paste("Interval", i))
  print(t.test(x,y, alternative = "less"))
}
```


# Multiple transcripts
Some genes have different transcripts that are regulated by same or different enhancers. Here we extract those genes and analyze them. 
## Extracting transcripts
First filtering out the multiple transcripts
```{r}
# Selecting rows from enhancer_transcript_df that contain significant transcripts
multiple_transcripts <-
  enhancer_transcript_df %>%
  filter(emp < 0.001)%>%
  select(grb, gene_trans, enh, transcript, ensembl, symbol, category) %>%
  unique() %>%
  group_by(ensembl) %>%
  filter( length(unique(ensembl)) < length(unique(transcript))) %>%
  mutate(num_of_transcripts = length(unique(transcript))) %>%
  group_by(transcript)

# For each transcript storing enhancers as a vector
trans_enh_vec <- multiple_transcripts %>%
  summarize(enh_vec=list(unique(enh)))

# Addinng the enhancer vector to the transcript
# Each row corresponds to one transcript
multiple_transcripts <-
  multiple_transcripts %>%
  left_join(trans_enh_vec) %>%
  select(everything(), -enh) %>%
  unique()%>%
  mutate(enh_num = lengths(enh_vec)) %>%
  ungroup
```

```{r}
# Helper function to calculate the ratio of TRUE instances in a vector
calcTruePerc <- function(vec){
  if(typeof(vec) != "logical"){
    stop("The vector is not a TRUE FALSE logical vector")
  }
  return(table(vec)["TRUE"]/length(vec))
}

# Modified is.element that returns the truePerc
isElementPerc <- function(x,y){
  return(calcTruePerc(is.element(x,y)))
}
```




Storing transcript comparisons in enh_overlap
```{r}
# Storing the result of the comparisons in a new column
multiple_transcripts$enh_overlaps <- NA

for(ensembl_id in multiple_transcripts %>% pull(ensembl) %>% unique()){
  
  working_gene <- multiple_transcripts %>%
    filter(ensembl == ensembl_id)
  
    # Store result in a matrix
    working_nrow <- nrow(working_gene)
    working_mat <- matrix(nrow = working_nrow, ncol = working_nrow)
    rownames(working_mat) <- working_gene$transcript
    colnames(working_mat) <- working_gene$transcript
    # Looping through elements tu build a matrix
    for (i in 1:working_nrow){
      for(j in 1:working_nrow){
        working_mat[i,j] <- 
          calcTruePerc(is.element(working_gene[i,]$enh_vec[[1]], working_gene[j,]$enh_vec[[1]])) 
      }
    }
    # Adding the overlap matrices to multiple transcritps
    for(i in 1:working_nrow){
      working_mat[is.na(working_mat)] <- 0
      multiple_transcripts[multiple_transcripts$transcript == working_gene[i,]$transcript,]$enh_overlaps <- list(working_mat)
    }
      
}
```




While exploring multiple transcripts I found that some genes stored in enhancer_transcript_df have more than one category because they are included in neighbouring GRBs. 
```{r}
genes_multiple_categories <- filter(enhancer_transcript_df, is.element(ensembl,enhancer_transcript_df %>% select(ensembl, category) %>% unique() %>% filter(duplicated(ensembl)) %>% pull(ensembl))) %>% select(ensembl, category, grb) %>% unique 


# write.csv(genes_multiple_categories, file ="data/MASTER_genes_with_multiple_categories.csv")    

multiple_transcripts %>%
  filter(!(is.element(ensembl, genes_multiple_categories$ensembl) & str_detect(category, "out")))

multiple_transcripts %>%
  filter(is.element(ensembl, genes_multiple_categories$ensembl) ) %>% View
```
